clue.text: Girl collected plants

definitions.meaning: the plants of a region taken together, its plant life

explanation.definitionFit: A girl's given name, and also the botanical word for all the plant life of an area.

clue.text: A publication to deliver to these parts

definitions.text: A publication to deliver to these parts

parts.words: A publication to deliver to these parts
parts.note: a newspaper pushed through local letterboxes at no charge to readers

explanation.surface: A local paper dropped through doors in the neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: A local newspaper given away without charge, paid for by its advertising.

clue.text: Nothing caught on river in William's original place

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
the Cam is the river through Cambridge

explanation.surface: A man named William was out for a duck by a river where he was born.
explanation.walkthrough: William of Ockham, the philosopher of the 'razor', was named after his Surrey village, also spelt this way.
explanation.definitionFit: The English village that gave its name to the medieval philosopher William, his birthplace.

clue.text: Spears a cat — how dramatic!

definitions.meaning: spears are the edible shoots of a vegetable
Gus the Theatre Cat in T. S. Eliot's cat poems has this as his full name

explanation.walkthrough: Gus, the Theatre Cat, in T. S. Eliot's Old Possum's Book of Practical Cats (the basis of the musical Cats), is short for this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A vegetable eaten as green shoots; and the full name of Eliot's actor cat Gus.

clue.text: Missing editor is without base

parts.note: something missing has not been found, so it is unfound

explanation.surface: A lost editor makes some claim baseless.
explanation.definitionFit: A claim without a basis or grounding is groundless, with nothing to support it.

clue.text: Released without a cover

definitions.meaning: released means set loose, freed from ties
a book with no binding has no cover

explanation.definitionFit: Untied and freed; and a book lacking its binding or covers.

clue.text: Outspokenness in play

definitions.meaning: frankness of speech, saying what one likes
play here is room to move, as a rope has play

explanation.definitionFit: Liberty to speak frankly; and the slack or room for movement in a mechanism.

clue.text: He used to teach pronouns

parts.note: us is a pronoun
her is another pronoun

explanation.surface: A former teacher of grammar.
explanation.walkthrough: One word, 'pronouns', supplies two pieces. An usher was once an assistant schoolmaster.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for an under-master or assistant schoolmaster.

clue.text: Doubt beef I'd left is altogether cooked

indicators.note: cooked says the letters are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone can't believe the leftover beef has been cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges BEEF, ID, L and IS; 'altogether' just links the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Refusal to believe; scepticism.

clue.text: Split deck needing planks? Precisely

parts.note: deal is pine or fir timber in planks
to a T means precisely

explanation.surface: A ship's deck that is cracked needs new boards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deck' looks nautical but is a pack of cards; to have split it among players is to have handed it out.
explanation.definitionFit: Cards handed out among the players: a pack shared round the table.

clue.text: Not certain bridge player's competent

parts.note: East is one of the four bridge players, abbreviated E, with the 's giving S
competent means capable

explanation.surface: Someone doubts a bridge player's competence.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players are named after compass points, so East is E; the possessive 's supplies the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be avoided or evaded is not inevitable, not a sure thing.

clue.text: Mount appearing not right to a prophetic bookmaker

indicators.note: R is right, and not right says that letter is dropped from the word for mount

parts.note: a mount is a horse that is ridden

explanation.surface: A horse is being backed with a racing bookie who claims to foresee results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bookmaker' looks like a betting man, but here it is the maker of a book of the Bible: a prophet who wrote one. 'not right' removes R from HORSE, leaving HOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor prophet of the Old Testament who gives his name to the book of his prophecies.

clue.text: Co-founder of ancient civilization backed another

indicators.note: backed says the co-founder's name is read from the end to the start

parts.note: Remus, with his twin Romulus, founded Rome in legend

explanation.surface: One founder of an old civilisation supports a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns REMUS round. 'another' is the definition: a second ancient civilisation besides Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: An early civilisation of Mesopotamia, the other old culture set beside Rome here.

clue.text: A French river bore

parts.note: un is French for 'a'
the Derwent is an English river

explanation.surface: A French river turns out to be dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' looks like a noun (a tidal wave on a river, or a dull person) but it is the past tense of bear. The Derwent is a river in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: To have borne something is to have suffered or experienced it, past tense matching past tense.

clue.text: Employed Old English, initially

indicators.note: initially says the English piece goes first, ahead of the word for old

parts.note: old means aged

explanation.surface: An Old English speaker was hired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' looks like a first-letter signal, but it orders the pieces: ENG comes at the start, before AGED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be employed is to be taken on or hired for work.

clue.text: Songs laid out for musical effect

indicators.note: laid out suggests the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: Songs set out to give a musical flourish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SONGS and LAID.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapid slide up or down a scale, played on harp, piano or trombone.

clue.text: One mass he composed, or another religious work

indicators.note: composed says the letters are put together in a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A composer wrote a mass, or perhaps another sacred piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' rearranges I, MASS and HE. A mass is one religious work; the answer is Handel's oratorio, another.
explanation.definitionFit: Handel's famous oratorio, a sacred choral composition like a mass.

clue.text: Friends overturned, apt to be careless

indicators.note: overturned says the word for friends is turned backwards

parts.note: pals are friends
happy can mean apt, as in a happy choice of words

explanation.surface: Friends knocked over by someone given to carelessness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' reverses PALS.
explanation.definitionFit: Casual and cheerfully irresponsible.

clue.text: Henry's short journey in gloomy conditions

parts.note: Hal is a familiar form of Henry
a flight is a short trip by air

explanation.surface: Henry's brief trip in dim weather.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Henry is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Dim, partial light such as at dusk.

clue.text: A double sink is good for these woollies

parts.note: a double is a twin
to sink is to set, as the sun does

explanation.surface: A double sink is just the place to wash knitwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sink' looks like a basin but is the verb: the sun sets, or sinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A matching jumper and cardigan worn together, a classic knitted outfit.

clue.text: Parched second fifteen's double round

indicators.note: round says the number goes around the second's letter

parts.note: twice fifteen is thirty

explanation.surface: A rugby second fifteen, parched, sets up a double round of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second fifteen' reads as a reserve rugby team, but second is S, and fifteen's double is THIRTY, which goes round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry and in need of a drink.

clue.text: Intimidated with loud scolding

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
an earful is a long telling-off

explanation.surface: Someone cowed by a loud telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone intimidated is frightened or afraid.

clue.text: Producer of original costumes to dress famous actor

parts.note: to fig out is to dress up
Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a famous Victorian actor-manager

explanation.surface: A wardrobe designer dresses a celebrated actor.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'original costumes' are the leaves Adam and Eve wore in Eden.
explanation.definitionFit: The tree whose leaves clothed Adam and Eve, the first garments.

clue.text: Calm conditions good for runners

definitions.meaning: calm here means relaxed and placid in temperament
in horse racing, ground that is ... suits the runners

explanation.definitionFit: A relaxed, placid nature; and racing ground that is easy for horses to run on.

clue.text: Last of ale tankards upended in bar

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word ale
upended in a down clue means the word for tankards is read bottom to top

parts.note: pots are drinking vessels such as tankards

explanation.surface: The dregs of beer in upturned mugs at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub but is the verb, in its legal sense of preclude.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal term for preventing someone from denying or asserting something.

clue.text: Short 3 to relish

parts.note: the cat in 3 down is better known by a short name, Gus

explanation.surface: A brief cross-reference to enjoyment.
explanation.walkthrough: In T. S. Eliot's cat poems the Theatre Cat's full name is shortened to Gus.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearty enjoyment or zest.

clue.text: It can accommodate some who telephone

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A place that will put up some callers.
explanation.definitionFit: A building offering rooms where guests can stay the night.

clue.text: Wild animal you can hear in these forests

indicators.note: you can hear says the word sounds like the name of the animal

parts.note: a tiger is a big wild cat

explanation.surface: A big cat might be heard prowling in the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: Siberian tigers do live in this northern coniferous forest.
explanation.definitionFit: The subarctic coniferous woodland of Siberia and Canada.

clue.text: Port is added to beer cask

indicators.note: added to says the word is joins on after the cask

parts.note: a tun is a large cask for beer or wine

explanation.surface: Port wine poured into a beer barrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the drink but is a harbour city, the capital of Tunisia.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Tunisia, a harbour city on the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Youth's second big increase

parts.note: multiplying by three is a big increase

explanation.surface: A young person grows hugely a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Youth' stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A young lad not yet fully grown.

clue.text: Get expert to classify pattern

parts.note: a pro is an expert
to classify is to type, sort by kind

explanation.surface: Bring in a specialist to sort out a design.
explanation.definitionFit: A model or original from which copies are made.

clue.text: Useful stuff for Baker Street, following old agreement

indicators.note: following says the street abbreviation comes after the old yes

parts.note: yea is an old word for yes

explanation.surface: Something handy for Baker Street, after an old deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Baker Street' reads as the London street of Sherlock Holmes, but Baker belongs to the definition: a baker uses this to raise bread.
explanation.definitionFit: The fungus a baker uses to make dough rise.
